highlights.title: Instagram's promise of 30 days' notice disappeared
highlights.text: In November 2024 the Instagram Terms of Use had two versions of the paragraph on changing the terms: one promising notice "at least 30 days" ahead, one with no minimum period. Every copy since, in the US version and others, has only the one without a minimum.

highlights.title: Two planned updates to Meta's business terms put on hold
highlights.text: By 6 November 2026 Meta had paused updates to its Self-Serve Ad Terms, due on 30 October, and its Commercial Terms, due on 20 November. Both pages now say the existing terms "remain in effect until further notice".

highlights.title: Advertisers' websites can be crawled for training
highlights.text: The Self-Serve Ad Terms rewritten in August 2025 say that placing an ad lets Meta "access, index, cache, analyze or crawl" the advertiser's websites, including for "research and training".

highlights.title: Conversations with Meta's AI now shape ads
highlights.text: From 16 December 2025 the Instagram Privacy Policy lists interactions with Meta's AI among the information used to personalise content and ads, and adds developing AI "for third parties" as a purpose. A banner announced the change in October.

highlights.title: Caps on creators' payouts and expiring ad credits
highlights.text: A 2026 rewrite of the Community Payment Terms lets Meta "impose or adjust caps on payouts of creators' earnings", charge another saved card when a payment fails and expire ad credits after three years.

highlights.title: Political spending pledges removed
highlights.text: Meta's political engagement page no longer says it makes no independent expenditures for or against candidates, or that the groups it funds may not use its money for political contributions.

changes.summary: A broad update. Users in the UK and outside the European region now contract with Meta Platforms, Inc. rather than Meta Platforms Ireland Limited for payments other than Meta-Processed Payments, and Meta may get information about users from third parties for tax and compliance purposes. Apple in-app purchasers now let Meta seek refunds from Apple for them, and Meta "will not be held liable" for losses from those refunds.
changes.headline: Moves UK and non-European users to Meta Platforms, Inc. for payments
